name: Kling Klang
ownershipStory: Kling Klang began as Kraftwerk's private studio, built and continually rebuilt by the band themselves, and became the imprint under which they controlled their own recordings and equipment. Owning the studio outright let Kraftwerk work at their own pace across years between releases and kept them almost entirely independent of outside production interference.
hook: Not really a record label in the usual sense. A studio Kraftwerk owned outright and never let anyone else run.

blurb.age7: This is Kraftwerk's own studio, which they built and owned themselves.
blurb.age13: Kling Klang is the name of Kraftwerk's own studio in Düsseldorf, which they built themselves and used to make every record. Because they owned it, nobody could rush them or tell them what to make.
blurb.adult: Kling Klang functioned less like a commercial label and more like total vertical control: studio, instruments, and masters all owned by the band. That independence is part of why Kraftwerk's discography is so small relative to their influence; they answered to no release schedule but their own.
